standard_prerequisites.name: Polychromatic colourings and the parameter m_H(k)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A polychromatic k-colouring of a hypergraph puts a vertex of every one of the k colour classes into every hyperedge; m_H(k) is the least m such that every member of the family has a polychromatic k-colouring after all edges of size below m are deleted, and it is infinity when no such m exists.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies both sides of the counted identity: the quantity m_A(k) that is being related to m_{A_s}(k), and the meaning of an edge that is not polychromatic.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: source lines 120 and 123-129, retained as context

standard_prerequisites.name: Definitional unpacking of the extremal value m_A(k)
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every m below m_A(k) there is a member of A together with a colouring under which no k-colouring of its m-edges is polychromatic; consequently, just below the exact value, such a member has a non-polychromatic edge of size at least m_A(k)-1, while the colouring witnessing m_A(k) makes every edge of size m_A(k) polychromatic.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proof takes one such extremal member and its non-polychromatic edge of size m_A(k)-1 and reuses the colouring of the reverse direction.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: source lines 680 and 682, read off the definition at source line 128

standard_prerequisites.name: Translated copies of a planar strip hypergraph along a diagonal
standard_prerequisites.statement: Finitely many translated copies of a finite planar point set can be placed along a diagonal so that every subset captured by an axis-parallel strip in the original set is captured by an axis-parallel strip in the copy, and so that any s of the copies lie inside the union of s axis-parallel strips.
standard_prerequisites.use: Realises the k(s-1)+1 copies used in the lower-bound direction and lets s extracted bad edges be read as one edge of the family A_s.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary finite counting and the pigeonhole principle
standard_prerequisites.statement: Among k(s-1)+1 objects coloured with k colours some colour occurs at least s times; and s(m-1)+1 points distributed over s sets leave one set with at least m points.
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the s copies with a common missing colour in the lower-bound direction and the single strip with m_A(k) points in the upper-bound direction.

core_obligations: Realise k(s-1)+1 translated copies of one extremal member of the strip family A along a diagonal, preserving every captured subset of the original point set as a captured subset of each copy.

In an arbitrary colouring of the resulting vertex set, extract from every copy a non-polychromatic edge of size m_A(k)-1, then pigeonhole the k(s-1)+1 copies over k colours to obtain s such edges that share one missing colour.

Read those s bad edges, one per copy, as a single edge of the family A_s of size s*m_A(k)-s that is not polychromatic, giving one inequality; then show that the colouring witnessing m_A(k) makes every edge of size s*m_A(k)-s+1 polychromatic, because such a set lies in a union of s strips and therefore contains m_A(k) points inside one strip.

proof_roadmap.step: Take an extremal member of A with a non-polychromatic edge of size m_A(k)-1 under any colouring, place k(s-1)+1 diagonal copies so that all original edges survive, and observe that every copy shows such an edge.
Pigeonhole the copies over the k colours to get s copies whose bad edges all miss the same colour; these s edges lie in the union of s axis-parallel strips, so m_{A_s}(k) is at least s*m_A(k)-s+1.
Conversely, reuse the colouring of A for edges of size s*m_A(k)-s+1: a set of that size inside a union of s strips contains m_A(k) points inside one strip, where all k colours already occur.

difficulty_reason: The counted object is an exact identity between two family parameters, m_{A_s}(k) = s*m_A(k)-s+1, where A_s is the family of unions of s axis-parallel strips (source lines 237-238) and m_A(k) is left as a black box, so both directions have to be derived from the definition of the two families rather than computed. The lower-bound direction at source line 680 needs a concrete realisation step that the statement alone does not suggest: k(s-1)+1 translated copies of one extremal member are placed along a diagonal so that every captured subset of the original set survives in the copy, and then two counting steps are chained, one pigeonhole over the copies to obtain s copies sharing a missing colour and one geometric reading of the s bad edges as a single edge of A_s of size s*m_A(k)-s. The reverse direction at source line 682 is short but easy to get wrong: an edge of the s-strip family must be split into its s strips, and only then does the pigeonhole give m_A(k) points inside one strip where all k colours are known to occur. Quoting the definition of m_A(k) without the diagonal copy construction and without the s-strip split yields neither inequality.

compared.difference: The only public item of this article is the infinite arithmetic-progression theorem about extendable difference sets, octant hypergraphs in R^3 and one infinite case. It never studies the family A_s of unions of s strips and no step of it is reused here.

The prepared strip target forbids 2-shallow hitting sets inside the m-uniform members of the primal family A by an eleven-cluster gadget. This target is an exact parameter identity for the larger family A_s of s-fold strip unions and is proved by diagonal copies plus pigeonhole; neither statement implies the other, and the shallow-hitting obstruction is not used.
The bottomless-rectangle target is a non-existence result for a different range family B with a two-case gadget; it shares neither the family, the parameter nor the proof technique with this item.

The companion card counted from the same article bounds the polychromatic parameter of the dual family A-star from below by a four-family missing-colour pigeonhole. This card instead determines the parameter of the s-fold union family A_s exactly, by diagonal copies of an extremal set; the two statements have different families, different conclusions and disjoint proofs.

editorial_scope: One counted exact parameter identity for unions of s axis-parallel strips, m_{A_s}(k) = s*m_A(k)-s+1, with both directions of the article's complete proof. The printed corollary specialising it, the primal strip and bottomless non-existence theorems, the A-plus and A-star bounds and both arithmetic-progression theorems are not counted.
